Core Theme
Making the invisible visible.

Every community has stories hiding in plain sight. This is a show built on a simple, stubborn idea — that data isn't just numbers. It's evidence of human lives, community decisions, policy outcomes, and the invisible systems shaping everyday existence. The goal isn't to teach people statistics. It's to help them see what they've been living through.

Behind every chartthere is a person.
Behind every statisticthere is a neighborhood.
Behind every trendthere is a human consequence.

What happens when we stop arguing about what we believe is happening — and start looking honestly at what the data is telling us?

The Mission

A public platform where data becomes human

Use storytelling, visualization, and conversation to help people understand the systems shaping their lives — and empower communities with the information needed to create change.

Eric's role on the show

"The person who walks into the room with the numbers everyone ignores — and asks: what story are these numbers trying to tell us?"

Eric Pachman

Founder, Data 4 The People · Co-Host

Eric Pachman is a data analyst, researcher, and founder who turns overlooked numbers into public accountability. A chemical engineer by training, his work spans healthcare, labor, and public policy — including analysis that helped surface roughly $225M in hidden Medicaid spending and shaped reforms in more than a dozen states — all rooted in transparency, rigor, and the belief that people deserve to understand the systems shaping their lives.

As founder and co-host of Data 4 The People, Eric brings that analyst's rigor to every story the show tells. He leads the research, builds the datasets, and uncovers what the numbers hide, grounding each episode in evidence and the questions that matter most. The data rarely gives up its truth easily — Eric is the one who digs until it does.

MBA — Harvard Business School ChE — University of Florida Co-founder · 46brooklyn Research 2026 O'Shaughnessy Fellow

Stefen Paris

Co-Host · Creative Director & Producer

Stefen Paris is a screenwriter, designer, and creative strategist who builds stories and experiences that make people feel something. His work spans live storytelling, community initiatives, and civic innovation, all rooted in culture, curiosity, and human connection.

As co-host and Creative Architect of Data 4 The People, Stefen brings that same storyteller's instinct to the world of data. He develops the season narrative, crafts episode arcs, curates guests, leads production, and shapes the show's creative identity, translating research into stories that resonate. If the data reveals the truth, Stefen helps people see themselves inside it.

Creative Director Producer & Story Translator Brand & Season Architecture Guest & Sponsor Strategy
Tone & Style

The audience should feel like they're in conversation with Eric about the future of society — never lectured at.

01Curious
02Human
03Thoughtful
04Challenging, not divisive
05Optimistic but realistic

Not this
"Here are the statistics."
But this

The Build of an Episode

Problem. Story. Data. Experts. Solutions.

One featured investigation per episode, told deeply — and never stopping at the problem. Every story moves the same way.

01

The Problem

Name the system that's failing people — food, work, care.

02

The Human Story

Someone living it: a caregiver, a shopper, a town emptying out.

03

The Data

Eric's research — what the numbers reveal, and what people misread.

04

The Experts

The people doing and studying the work, in conversation — not quoted at a distance.

05

Solutions

Where every episode lands. What could actually change.

"We don't stop at identifying the problem. We ask what we do about it — that's what separates this from traditional journalism."

~5 minClosing
A powerful story or questionExperts, solutions + a challenge to carry forward
The Spine of the Series

Five questions the show keeps returning to

01

Data as a Public Good

Who has access to information? Who controls the narrative? Why public data and transparency build the trust a society runs on.
AccessTransparencyTrust
02

The Hidden Economics of Everyday Life

Housing, labor, education, healthcare, transportation, opportunity. "What systems determine someone's future before they ever make a decision?"
03

The Geography of Opportunity

How where you live shapes income, education, health, and mobility — with maps treated as a character in the show.
MapsMobilityPlace
04

Numbers vs. Understanding

Why people see the same statistics and walk away with opposite conclusions — and how visualization can build shared understanding instead.
05

Restoring Shared Truth

In an era where everyone has their own information source, can data still create common ground?
Season One

Seeing America Clearly

Eight episodes, one arc. We open with the story behind Data 4 The People, then go deep on the three systems that quietly decide American life — food, work, and care — two episodes each, always moving from the problem to what we actually do about it. We close by asking where the country goes from here.

EP 01 · PROLOGUE

The Story Behind Data 4 The People

Why Eric built this — from chemical engineer to data storyteller — what he believes is broken in how America understands its own problems, and why speaking, not just writing, creates the connection that changes minds.

Central questionWhat happens when a society loses the ability to agree on reality?
Pillar I

Food Assistance & SNAP

Problem → Solution · 2 episodes
EP 02Source ↗

A War We Stopped Fighting

SNAP, food deserts, and the Thrifty Food Plan — why access to food assistance depends more on your zip code than your income.

The problemHas America quietly given up on the War on Poverty?
Read the investigation ↗
EP 03Source ↗

1.2 Cheetos a Day

What the government's food budget actually buys — down to about two Cheetos a week per person — and what real accountability, and a fix, would look like.

Toward solutionsIf a benefit can't feed a family, whose job is it to say so?
Read the investigation ↗
Pillar II

The Disappearing Workforce

Problem → Solution · 2 episodes
EP 04Source ↗

The Map That Went Viral

The structural labor-force decline hollowing out non-metro America — sixteen years of it, county by county — and why the map struck such a nerve.

The problemWhat happens when a community slowly disappears?
Read the investigation ↗
EP 05Source ↗

The Spreading Map

How decline moves county to county like a contagion, reaching places that once felt safe — and what actually keeps a town alive when the young people leave.

Toward solutionsCan a place come back once it starts to empty out?
Read the investigation ↗
Pillar III

The Coming Age of Elder Care

Problem → Solution · 2 episodes
EP 06Source ↗

Healthcare Becomes Eldercare

The flip side of the shrinking workforce: as America ages, demand for care surges. The same demographic shift, seen from the other direction.

The problemWho cares for us when there aren't enough of us left to do it?
Read the investigation ↗
EP 07Source ↗

The 2027 Cliff

The care economy runs on Medicaid — and the cuts arriving in 2027 threaten caregivers, families, and the fragile system holding aging America together.

Toward solutionsWhat happens to the people who do the caring when the money disappears?
Read the investigation ↗
EP 08 · FINALE

Where America Goes From Here

Pulling the three threads together — food, work, and care — into one honest question about the country's future, and a doorway into the next season.

Closing questionIf we can finally see the problem clearly, do we have the will to fix it?
